## Not One System This Time

<!-- STEP id="two-separate-diagrams" -->
The last lesson's two boxes moved the same direction. One system, one equation, straightforward.

These two blocks move opposite ways: one down, one up.

So draw two separate free-body diagrams, one for each block.

<!-- STEP id="mass-1-fbd" -->
## Block 1: 5 kg, Moving Down

Two forces act on it: weight $m_1g$ pulling down, tension $T$ pulling up.

Call 'down' positive for this block — that's the way it's actually going.

$$m_1g - T = m_1a$$

<!-- STEP id="mass-2-fbd" -->
## Block 2: 3 kg, Moving Up

Two forces act on it too: weight $m_2g$ pulling down, tension $T$ pulling up.

Call 'up' positive for this block — that's the way it's actually going.

$$T - m_2g = m_2a$$

Both blocks share the same $a$. The string doesn't stretch, so whatever distance one falls, the other rises.

<!-- STEP id="eliminate-tension" -->
## Adding the Two Equations

Two equations, two unknowns — $T$ and $a$. Just like solving simultaneous linear equations.

Add them. $T$ cancels.

$$a = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2}$$

<!-- STEP id="find-tension" -->
## Finding the Tension

Substitute $a$ back into either original equation.

$$T = m_2(g + a) = m_1(g - a)$$

**Different objects get different equations — combined with algebra, not just added together like last lesson's system.**
